lookups.why: Search for direct published evidence linking this site or element to neuroblastoma or its proposed regulatory mechanism.

games.reason: Both chains have a highly expressed TF with a SK-N-SH ChIP-seq summit near the variant, but the GATA-family binding prediction is substantially stronger and more consistent: six of six models pass the gate, with a strong ref-over-alt effect. The nuclear-receptor signal is weaker (two of 29 models pass) and predicts alt-over-ref binding. These are in-vitro predictions, not allele-specific occupancy measurements; they do not establish either disease mechanism.

Both chains have a similar near-variant ChIP-seq summit and the same element and LMO1 context. B is better supported at the binding link: the GATA2 model strongly predicts greater binding to ref C (E13), and GATA2 is expressed with a summit 32 bp from the variant in SK-N-SH. A’s alt-favoring signal is from a nuclear-receptor family model, while RARA’s own model does not pass the gate and instead modestly favors ref C (E14, E25); this fits A’s RARA-specific claim less directly.
